scenes.headline: How diffusion builds Minecraft worlds from block IDs
scenes.sub: Dream-Cubed, and why a hand-placed block comes out exactly.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Apricot! Dream-Cubed runs diffusion directly on Minecraft's block IDs. Here's why that makes inpainting free.

scenes.text: Treat blocks as tokens and diffuse by masking them. A block you place by hand is never masked, so the model builds around it exactly.
scenes.say: Blocks are tokens, and diffusion masks them. A block you place by hand is never masked, so the model builds around it exactly.

steps.label: Every voxel is a block ID
steps.note: 117 block types in the core set
steps.say: Each chunk is thirty-two blocks a side, and every voxel is an integer block ID: dirt, water, stone.

steps.label: Mask voxels one by one, predict them
steps.say: Training masks each voxel independently, more as time goes on, and the network predicts every masked block.

steps.label: Sampling starts fully masked
steps.say: Sampling starts from a fully masked chunk, and unmasks it over a fixed number of steps.

steps.label: Your blocks are never masked
steps.say: Blocks you place by hand are left out of the masking at every step. The model builds around them, exactly.

scenes.title: Why a continuous model can't do this

left.title: Continuous DDPM
items: Noises every voxel on one schedule
A clamped clean block reads as zero noise
left.say: A continuous DDPM noises every voxel on one schedule. Clamp a placed block clean, and the model sees zero noise where it expects some.

right.title: Masked MD4
items: Fixed voxels never enter the corruption
right.say: Masked diffusion has no mismatch. The fixed voxel was never part of the corruption, so it cannot drift.

scenes.title: Outpainting is the same trick, tiled

items.text: Split the world into overlapping cells
items.say: For a bigger world, split the canvas into overlapping cells.
Generate the first cell from scratch.
After that, each cell's overlap with its finished neighbours is fixed context, never masked.
A five-by-five world takes over an hour of H100 time, one cell after another.

scenes.label: adjusted FID, MD4 against DDPM at patch 2: a statistical tie
scenes.note: they split at patch 4, where DDPM fails outright
scenes.say: On the paper's own metric, the two tie. They split at patch size four, where DDPM fails outright.

scenes.text: Diffuse in the game's own tokens, and masking turns inpainting into a guarantee instead of an add-on.

recap: Blocks are tokens, and diffusion masks them
Outpainting reuses the trick, cell by cell
scenes.say: To recap: block tokens, masking that skips your blocks, and outpainting from the same trick.
